text:
ash.k: repro on staging — quick org-switch + rollout fallback shows other org's run rows in the console UI. happened twice in a row. attaching steps + small console network trace :eyes:

priya: ow. can you paste the steps and the trace? is this only when a rollout fallback happens or any fallback?

ash.k: steps:
1) log in as org-A, open /console/runs
2) open a long-running run, switch to org-B quickly via workspace switcher
3) trigger a route fallback (simulated by killing model pool node)
4) UI sporadically renders 2-3 rows owned by org-A while showing org-B context

network trace shows the internal call to `/internal/runs/list` returning rows with no `x-tenant-id` in request:
```
GET /internal/runs/list HTTP/1.1
Host: internal-api.svc
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Accept: application/json
# NOTE: missing x-tenant-id header here when fallback path used
```

kevin: that matches my suspicion — the router fallback path strips/forgets tenant-tag when proxying to the global cache. it then serves cached rows without tenant scoping. :bug:

migs: we also saw quota attribution flips when the header is missing; usage ends up on the wrong org. telemetry currently aggregates per-request auth token but not per-response rows served by tenant, so misses this class.

sre-bot: incident INC-4821 created (severity: P2) — tag: multi-tenant-ui-leak. Assigned: eng-platform

priya: short-term mitigation: prevent UI from rendering rows unless row.owner_org === currentOrg in client. but that's brittle if the server sent wrong rows (still a data leak).

kevin: agreed. server-side enforcement is the real fix: internal-api must require `x-tenant-id` (or validated token-scoped tenant) on endpoints that return tenant-scoped data. fail closed (401) if missing. also add a router middleware that preserves the header on fallback and logs when a header is omitted.

Suggested middleware (pseudo):
```
function enforceTenantHeader(req, res, next) {
  if (!req.headers['x-tenant-id']) return res.status(401).send('missing tenant');
  next();
}
```

ash.k: i'll open a tiny PR with middleware + an integration test that simulates fallback. i'll also add a console-level assert to hide rows if org mismatch, as a defense-in-depth. assigning PR to migs. link when ready. :+1:

migs: taking it. i'll also add a canary probe that does a tenant-identity check during rollout (health check must include `GET /internal/runs/list` with explicit tenant and assert results contain that tenant's rows only).

priya: telemetry ask: add a per-tenant metric `console.rows.served` with tag `owner_org` and `requesting_org`. alert if `owner_org != requesting_org` for any non-zero count. also add a daily regression eval that runs tenant-switch scenarios in staging and asserts zero cross-tenant rows.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary job queued for staging: redwood/console-canary (includes tenant-auth-check). ETA ~10m.

ash.k: thanks everyone. plan: PR for middleware + test (ash.k -> migs), server require header, UI guard deployed as hotfix, telemetry alert + e2e. we'll triage INC-4821 and keep channel updated.

kevin: after this, let's do a short postmortem and add a lint for internal-sdk: make tenant header required in the typed client so callers cannot accidentally omit it. :memo:

ash.k: noted. i'll include the internal-sdk change in the same PR series.
